text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- World praises King Hussein's initiative to save Middle East peace process. Prime Minister Kabariti puts Egyptian President Mubarak in picture about king's efforts to give impetus to peace.

- Jordan-EU cooperation agreement likely to be delayed. Planning Ministry official says EU demanding that Jordan take responsibility for all Arab refugees seeking asylum in Europe from Jordan. "These conditions violate our national sovereignty".
- Three ministers oppose draft law on duties of national security court.
- Prime Minister Kabariti and Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister Aziz discuss economic cooperation and ways of developing it.
- Three Jordanians imprisoned in Israel are released and cross back into Jordan.
- Sources say Iraq requests $30 million worth of Jordanian medicines under U.N.-approved oil-for-food deal.
- Peace process is in new phase, Information Minister Muasher says. Kabariti says peace is back on track.
- Iraq will continue oil supply to Jordan, "technical details" delaying renewal of deal, Aziz says.
